programme.title: Planet Earth III
programme.desc: The third part of the nature documentary, produced over almost five years, concludes the trilogy almost two decades after the first series was broadcast.Its creators used pioneering film technologies, including:light drones, super-fast cameras and remotely controlled deep-sea submarines.In eight episodes, viewers will visit the most remote jungles, the darkest ocean depths, the world's largest caves and the hottest deserts and steppes.They will learn the story about nature's will to survive and the adaptive abilities of various species.The Earth is at a tipping point and changes in the natural world are felt in every ecosystem and affect numerous creatures.The series highlights the growing need to protect and restore nature.In the last episode, viewers will meet inspiring people from various corners of the world who are the face of change and saving the Earth.They are committed to risking their lives to protect the planet.Sir David Attenborough will guide the series.

programme.title: Blue Planet 2
programme.desc: In Southeast Asia there is the so-calledThe Coral Triangle, an area containing the richest reef in the world.In this vibrant place, there is constant competition for space, food and a mate.Coral reefs, which cover less than 1/10 percent of the ocean floor, support 1/4 of known marine species.Corals create complex and diverse structures.Each reef also has a clearly marked boundary beyond which lies the ocean depth.It is a kind of wall that protects the city from waves.The reefs are inhabited by, among others:cuttlefish that prey on crabs.Although this crustacean's pincers pose a great threat, cuttlefish have an extraordinary weapon - their skin contains millions of pigment cells that create constantly changing patterns.Creatures that have adapted well to life in reefs that resemble underwater cities reap many benefits.

programme.title: Eden: Untamed Planet
programme.desc: Documentary filmmakers go to the most remote corners of our planet to discover the secrets of the few untouched ecosystems.From the Namib Desert to Patagonia, only a few places on Earth have remained largely unchanged.Isolated from the rest of the world, they managed to defend themselves against the most harmful effects of human interference.Life there goes on as nature intended.The creators will take viewers on an exciting journey to the last places that are paradise on earth.Amazing, breathtaking landscapes will be presented, as well as exciting behaviors of the most popular animals in the world.Each episode will feature a different unique corner of the globe - from the mysterious, fog-shrouded forests of Borneo to the lush beauty of Africa's Luangwa floodplain Only 500 years ago, the first sailors reached the Galapagos Islands.Seeing mountain peaks shrouded in fog, picturesque beaches and creatures resembling mythical beasts, they thought they had arrived in a magical land.To get there, each colonizer had to make a thousands-kilometer journey across the Pacific.Galapagos fur lions were one of the few mammals to do this.They came here two million years ago from North American waters.Life in the Galapagos waters thrives on powerful ocean currents.The animals have long traveled underwater from the Southern Ocean.The most impressive coasts of the archipelago are located on the island of Fernandina, one of the most pristine in the world.It is called the land of dragons because 120,000 marine iguanas live here.

programme.title: Eden: Untamed Planet
programme.desc: Documentary filmmakers go to the most remote corners of our planet to discover the secrets of the few untouched ecosystems.From the Namib Desert to Patagonia, only a few places on Earth have remained largely unchanged.Isolated from the rest of the world, they managed to defend themselves against the most harmful effects of human interference.Life there goes on as nature intended.The creators will take viewers on an exciting journey to the last places that are paradise on earth.Amazing, breathtaking landscapes will be presented, as well as exciting behaviors of the most popular animals in the world.Each episode will feature a different unique corner of the globe - from the mysterious, fog-shrouded forests of Borneo to the lush beauty of Africa's Luangwa floodplain Documentarians start their journey high in the Andes.A chain of mountain peaks stretches along Patagonia, shaping life in this mysterious land.To the north, in their shadow, lies one of the driest and most inhospitable deserts in the world - the Atacama.This is an area of ​​over 100,000 square kilometers.In some places, rainfall has not been recorded for five hundred years.At an altitude of 4,800 m above sea levelultraviolet radiation is so strong that human skin can burn in just a few moments.However, there will be those who feel like they are in paradise here.Every spring, thousands of flamingos arrive from southern Patagonia.They land in shallow lagoons to feed on the abundant algae and brine shrimp that give them their characteristic pink color.
